title: The plus construction computes sheafification
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal F^+$ be its plus construction and $\theta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^+$ the canonical map [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]: $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, the colimit over the coverings $\mathcal U$ of $U$ and their refinements of the sets $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ of families $(s_i)\in\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)$ with $s_i|_{U_i\times_UU_j}=s_j|_{U_i\times_UU_j}$; it is a presheaf and $\theta_{\mathcal F}$ a morphism of presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf]. Put $\mathcal F^{++}=(\mathcal F^+)^+$ and $\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F^+}\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^{++}$. Then (Stacks Sites, Theorem 00WB and Proposition 00WH): (1) $\mathcal F^+$ is separated and the canonical map $\theta_{\mathcal F^+}:\mathcal F^+\to\mathcal F^{++}$ is injective, as in [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-separated]; (2) $\mathcal F^{++}$ is a sheaf; (3) $\theta^2_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^{++}$ is a sheafification: for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal C$ and every morphism of presheaves $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ there is a unique morphism $\varphi':\mathcal F^{++}\to\mathcal G$ with $\varphi'\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\varphi$. Consequently, if $\theta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\#$ is the universal-property sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], there is a unique isomorphism $\mathcal F^{++}\simeq\mathcal F^\#$ of presheaves carrying $\theta^2_{\mathcal F}$ to $\theta$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification): Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), parts (1)--(4), Definition 00WG (definition-associated-sheaf) and Proposition 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint) with its proof

proof.text: Part (1). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-separated] to $\mathcal F$ gives that $\mathcal F^+$ is separated (for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ the map $\mathcal F^+(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal F^+(U_i)$ is injective; injectivity into the equalizer of the two maps to $\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F^+(U_i\times_UU_j)$, as that node phrases it, is the same condition since the equalizer is a subset of the product) and that $\theta_{\mathcal F^+}:\mathcal F^+\to\mathcal F^{++}$ is injective.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB(1) (item-sep, tag 00WC), and 00WB(2) applied to the separated presheaf $\mathcal F^+$

proof.text: Part (2). By step 1, $\mathcal F^+$ is a separated presheaf of sets in the sense of Sites, Definition 00WA. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-of-separated-is-sheaf] to $\mathcal G=\mathcal F^+$ (a presheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf]) gives that $(\mathcal F^+)^+=\mathcal F^{++}$ is a sheaf.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB(4) (item-plusplus) and its proof ('now obvious' from (1) and (2))

proof.text: Part (3), existence. Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-of-sheaf-iso], $\theta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^+$ is an isomorphism, so $\mathcal G^+$ is a sheaf (a presheaf isomorphic to a sheaf is a sheaf, the equalizer condition being transported by the isomorphism), and applying the same node to $\mathcal G^+$, $\theta_{\mathcal G^+}$ is an isomorphism; hence $\theta^2_{\mathcal G}=\theta_{\mathcal G^+}\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^{++}$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-functorial](b) applied to $\varphi$ and to $\varphi^+:\mathcal F^+\to\mathcal G^+$ we have $\theta_{\mathcal G}\circ\varphi=\varphi^+\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}$ and $\theta_{\mathcal G^+}\circ\varphi^+=\varphi^{++}\circ\theta_{\mathcal F^+}$, with $\varphi^{++}=(\varphi^+)^+$; composing, $\theta^2_{\mathcal G}\circ\varphi=\varphi^{++}\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}$. Put $\varphi'=(\theta^2_{\mathcal G})^{-1}\circ\varphi^{++}:\mathcal F^{++}\to\mathcal G$; then $\varphi'\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=(\theta^2_{\mathcal G})^{-1}\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal G}\circ\varphi=\varphi$.

source.place: Sites, Proposition 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), proof: the commutative diagram from Lemma 00W5 and Theorem 00WB(3)

proof.text: Part (3), uniqueness. Let $\varphi',\varphi'':\mathcal F^{++}\to\mathcal G$ with $\varphi'\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\varphi''\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}$, and let $x\in\mathcal F^{++}(U)$. Local surjectivity of $\theta$ (Sites, Lemma 00W9): by [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](1) applied to $\mathcal F^+$, $x=[\mathcal U,(t_i)_i]$ for a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $(t_i)\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^+)$, and by part (3) of the same node (with $h:U_i\to U$ factoring through $U_i$ via the identity) $x|_{U_i}=\theta_{\mathcal F^+}(t_i)$. Likewise each $t_i=[\{U_{ik}\to U_i\}_k,(r_{ik})_k]$ with $r_{ik}\in\mathcal F(U_{ik})$ and $t_i|_{U_{ik}}=\theta_{\mathcal F}(r_{ik})$. Since $\theta_{\mathcal F^+}$ is a morphism of presheaves, $x|_{U_{ik}}=\theta_{\mathcal F^+}(t_i|_{U_{ik}})=\theta^2_{\mathcal F}(r_{ik})$, so $\varphi'(x)|_{U_{ik}}=\varphi'(\theta^2_{\mathcal F}(r_{ik}))=\varphi''(\theta^2_{\mathcal F}(r_{ik}))=\varphi''(x)|_{U_{ik}}$. The family $\{U_{ik}\to U\}_{i,k}$ is a covering of $U$ by axiom (ii) of a site, and a sheaf is separated (the map $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod\mathcal G(U_{ik})$ is injective by the equalizer condition), so $\varphi'(x)=\varphi''(x)$. Hence $\varphi'=\varphi''$.

source.place: Sites, Proposition 00WH, proof ('uniqueness follows from Lemma 00W9'), with Lemma 00W9 (lemma-plus-surjective) and its proof

proof.text: Comparison with $\mathcal F^\#$. By steps 2--4, $(\mathcal F^{++},\theta^2_{\mathcal F})$ is a sheaf with a morphism from $\mathcal F$ through which every morphism from $\mathcal F$ to a sheaf factors uniquely, which is the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. By the universal properties there are unique morphisms $a:\mathcal F^{++}\to\mathcal F^\#$ with $a\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\theta$ and $b:\mathcal F^\#\to\mathcal F^{++}$ with $b\circ\theta=\theta^2_{\mathcal F}$; then $b\circ a\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\mathrm{id}\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}$ gives $b\circ a=\mathrm{id}$ by the uniqueness for $\mathcal F^{++}$, and likewise $a\circ b=\mathrm{id}$. So $a$ is an isomorphism carrying $\theta^2_{\mathcal F}$ to $\theta$, and it is the only morphism with $a\circ\theta^2_{\mathcal F}=\theta$.

source.place: Sites, the paragraph after Proposition 00WH (the sheafification is unique up to unique isomorphism; left adjoint to the inclusion)

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks Sites Section 00W1 (Theorem 00WB, Definition 00WG, Proposition 00WH; tags checked in tags/tags). The statement defined F^+ ad hoc as classes of families whose pullbacks agree only after a further covering of U_i x_U U_j, which is not Stacks's H^0 condition (exact agreement on U_i x_U U_j); it now uses the plus construction node def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction (colimit over J_U) created by the split of lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-separated, cites lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf for F^+ being a presheaf, makes the canonical map theta^2 explicit and states the universal property of clause (3) (Stacks Prop. 00WH, not part of 00WB). Proof in five steps: (1) by the separated node; (2) by the new node 'G separated => G^+ sheaf' (00WB(2)); (3) existence via functoriality (new node, Lemma 00W5) and 'G sheaf => G -> G^+ iso' (new node, 00WB(3)); (4) uniqueness via local surjectivity (parts (1),(3) of the presheaf node, i.e. Lemma 00W9) and separatedness of sheaves; (5) unique iso with F^# by universal properties (elementary). Mathlib has all of this for plusObj over covering sieves (Plus.lean, ConcreteSheafification.lean, LeftExact.lean), recorded as candidates, not leaves, since the family/sieve identification is a theorem.

lean.statement: theorem plus_sheafification_theorem {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition] [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u w)) : (∀ (U : C) (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (s s' : (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).obj (op U)), (∀ i : E.I₀, (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).map (E.f i).op s = (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).map (E.f i).op s') → s = s') ∧ (∀ U : C, Function.Injective ((J.toGrothendieck.toPlus (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P)).app (op U))) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf J.toGrothendieck (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P)) ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w))) (φ : P ⟶ G.obj), ∃! φ' : J.toGrothendieck.plusObj (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P) ⟶ G.obj, (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P ≫ J.toGrothendieck.toPlus (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P)) ≫ φ' = φ) ∧ (∀ (Q : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w))) (θ : P ⟶ Q.obj), (∀ (G : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w))) (φ : P ⟶ G.obj), ∃! ψ : Q.obj ⟶ G.obj, θ ≫ ψ = φ) → ∃! e : J.toGrothendieck.plusObj (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P) ≅ Q.obj, (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P ≫ J.toGrothendieck.toPlus (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P)) ≫ e.hom = θ)
